title: Fever in a newborn: when is it urgent?
summary: A temperature in a young baby needs quick attention. Here's how to think about it.
whatsNormal:
A normal temperature is typically around 97.7–99.5°F (36.5–37.5°C) rectally, depending on the method you use.

A fever is usually 100.4°F (38°C) or higher rectally.

In babies under 3 months, fever is taken seriously because their immune systems are still developing. That does not mean every warm forehead is an emergency, but it does mean you should not wait and see for days.
watchFor: Baby feels warm but you do not have a thermometer, get one and recheck
Poor feeding, unusual sleepiness, or irritability with a warm temperature
Fever after recent vaccines, some low-grade fever can be expected; ask your clinician what to watch for
callDoctorIf: Any fever 100.4°F (38°C) or higher in a baby under 3 months, call now
Fever with rash, difficulty breathing, or blue lips
You cannot reach your pediatrician and baby is under 3 months with fever, go to ER
Seizure, limpness, or you cannot wake baby

triage.intro: Answer a few quick questions. This is educational guidance, not a diagnosis.

green.title: Likely OK to watch
green.body: No fever by your check and baby seems well. Keep monitoring temperature and hydration. Call your pediatrician if anything changes or you are worried.

yellow.title: Call your pediatrician today
yellow.body: Some signs need a clinician's input even if it is not an emergency. Describe symptoms, how you measured temperature, and when they started.

red.title: Seek care now
red.body: Fever in a young baby or concerning symptoms need prompt medical evaluation. Call your pediatrician now or go to the emergency department if you cannot reach them.

age.question: Is your baby younger than 3 months?

well.question: Is your baby feeding, alert enough to wake for feeds, and not having breathing difficulty?
